DISPLACED ONE-HERALD FOLLOWUP — CONSTRUCTIVE COEFFICIENT EVALUATION
Date: 10 October 2026. Supplemental branch, frozen v2 code unchanged.
Status: internally reconstructed proof and completed supplemental sampler; independent model audits completed. Authoritative endpoint review: ../gaussian_software_audit/displaced/report.txt. Coefficient proof review: ../gaussian_displaced_audit/report.txt. No external/formal verification or historical novelty claim. The earlier displaced_gate.txt accurately refuted a naive single-unimodal-envelope route; it is superseded as a claim that no constructive route is available.

THE DECISIVE CHANGE
A two-saddle Fourier local-CLT approximation is unnecessary. Fold the real Gaussian moment integral onto the positive half-line. This combines the parity-related saddles before numerical approximation and leaves a positive integrand, including arbitrarily small displacement at odd n. Its normalized width and complex analyticity bounds are uniform in the coefficient order and displacement.

COEFFICIENT THEOREM
Let a,c>=0 be rational, n>=0 an integer encoded in binary, and p>=1. Write H_n=[z^n]exp(a z^2/2+c z). There is a deterministic algorithm polynomial in total coefficient input length L, log(n+1), and p which either recognizes H_n=0 or produces an enclosure of log H_n of absolute width<=2^(-p). Equivalently one obtains a relative-accuracy enclosure in floating mantissa/exponent representation. Exact rational H_n is not the output: its numerator/denominator may require Omega(n) bits.
Zero/elementary cases: H_0=1; a=0 gives c^n/n!; c=0 gives H_even=(a/2)^(n/2)/(n/2)! and H_odd=0; a=c=0 handled directly.

POSITIVE INTEGRAL IDENTITY
For a,c>0, set d=c/sqrt(a), s=(-1)^n and m=(d+sqrt(d^2+4n))/2. Then m>=sqrt(n), m>=d and m-d=n/m. Since n!H_n is the n-th moment of N(c,a),
 H_n = a^(n/2)/(n!sqrt(2pi)) integral_0^infty t^n exp[-(t-d)^2/2] b_s(t) dt,
 b_s(t)=1+s exp(-2dt).
For even n the bracket is positive and >=1. For odd n it is positive for t>0 and equals -expm1(-2dt). There is no subtraction of two large integrated quantities.
Normalize at m:
 G(t)=exp{n[log(t/m)-(t-m)/m]-(t-m)^2/2} b_s(t)/b_s(m),
 I=integral_0^infty G(t)dt.
The prefactor can be evaluated stably in logarithms:
 log H_n=(n/2)log a-logGamma(n+1)-(1/2)log(2pi)+n log m
          -(1/2)(n/m)^2+log b_s(m)+log I.
Using m-d=n/m avoids subtracting close large numbers.

2. SINGLE-HERALD GAUSSIAN COUNT COMPILER: UNDISPLACED BASELINE

Contract: rational, symmetric, entrywise nonnegative Bargmann kernel K with
ket/bra exchange symmetry, spectral radius rho(XK)<1, and globally zero
displacement. For a physical interpretation the kernel must describe a valid
density operator; positivity of its entries alone does not certify physicality.
One physical mode is observed at a nonzero-probability photon event h, encoded
in binary. Return the remaining count vector in binary to requested TV error
epsilon. The theorem does not cover arbitrary complex/signed kernels, multiple
herald modes, or displacement coupled into the herald.

Eliminate the unobserved doubled modes using rational Schur operations. The
effective herald matrix is [[a,b],[b,a]]. If k is the number of cross pairs,
then k=h modulo two and its unnormalized weight is
  w(k)=h!^2 a^(h-k)b^k /
       [k! 2^(h-k) (((h-k)/2)!)^2].
Its consecutive ratio is
  w(k+2)/w(k)=(b/a)^2 (h-k)^2/[(k+1)(k+2)],
which decreases. Exact ratio comparisons locate a mode using O(log(h+1))
comparisons. A dyadic rejection envelope samples this one integer using
certified log-factorial ratios, without constructing h tokens or an h-sized
factorial. Reverse Schur sampling then reconstructs aggregate counts using
binomial and negative-binomial laws. The loop shape is 1/2 plus the routed
edge count; omitting that count would be incorrect.

The ideal finite-bit construction has polynomial cost in the complete rational
input length, number of modes, log(h+1), and log(1/epsilon), using certified
polynomial-time elementary-function evaluations. Graph operations, stored
routing coefficients, and the number of scalar calls are O(modes^3). Small
Schur pivots and large output counts are charged through their bit lengths.
The implementation uses FLINT/Arb ball arithmetic. Its enclosure logic and
randomness caps were audited, but a uniform polynomial performance proof for
the actual Arb refinement implementation has not been supplied. Timings are
observations, not such a proof.

The final endpoint allocates epsilon/4 to capped uniform-integer ticket draws,
3epsilon/8 to the matching law, and 3epsilon/8 across reverse scalar calls.

fixed pair orientation after physical marking identification, alpha=1/2,
ket/bra count summation, and the globally undisplaced single-herald compression
all admit independent complete algebraic derivations under the stated input
promises. The count-length and scalar precision claims also have a polynomial
bit route described below. This is an internal reconstruction, not external
verification, formal proof, universal software certification, or novelty.

The source already excludes its most tempting overextensions: nonnegative
coefficients alone do not certify a quantum density operator; encoded exact
rational data do not supply tomography; conditional simulation does not make
physical heralds occur. Preserve those premises in all downstream claims.

1. CONDITIONAL GAUSSIAN IDENTITY
Let the Bargmann series be R(u)=c exp(u^T K u/2+ell^T u), K symmetric.
The diagonal physical Fock coefficient for n is
  (partial_(ket)^n partial_(bra)^n R)(0) / product_i n_i!.
There is one factorial per physical mode, not two. For unobserved modes,
tracing with physical mark z_i is the formal contraction operator
  exp[(1/2) partial_U^T C_z partial_U],   C_z=D_z X_U=X_U D_z.
The equality requires the same z_i on ket and bra copies. It follows directly
from the coefficient of (partial_ket_i partial_bra_i)^n/n!.

For any symmetric formal covariance C, the Gaussian contraction identity is
  exp[(1/2)partial^T C partial] exp(x^T A x/2+b^T x)|_(x=0)
